# Policy-Conditioned Constrained Decoding for Column-Level Access Control in Text-to-SQL

[All reading notes](../reading-notes.md) · [Catalog entry](../README.md#pcc-sql)

**Full paper read · 2026-11-11**

[Original source](https://aclanthology.org/2026.aacl-long.239.pdf) · AACL-IJCNLP 2026 proceedings, pages 5377–5391; complete 15-page publisher PDF.

**Reading coverage:** All 15 PDF pages: Sections 1–8, limitations, references and Appendices A–H; all prompts, decoding details, policy-construction rules and Tables 1–11. Figures 1–2 were visually inspected. Artifact source and license inspection was textual only.

**Additional inspected sources:** [Official implementation and release notes](https://github.com/yamanalab/pcc-sql) · [Verified Spider-CU policy/refusal records](https://github.com/yamanalab/pcc-sql/blob/main/data/dev.json) · [MIT code license text](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yamanalab/pcc-sql/main/LICENSE) · [Preprint identity/version record](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.12341)

## Research question

Database interfaces must refuse or adapt requests when the allowed use of a column depends on whether it is projected, filtered, joined or aggregated.

## Method

PCC-SQL tracks grammar roles and scope, masks disallowed column tokens and emits REFUSE when continuation is blocked, validation fails or syntax is unsupported. Four permission types distinguish public, condition-only, aggregate-only and hidden columns.

## Evaluation

Three open models are compared with prompting, retry, verification and rollback on Spider-CU, BIRD-CU and Spider-ACL. Synthetic policies use column-name rules and reference-query usage. Coverage measures compliant output; execution match is separately measured only on SQL-gold cases. Spider-ACL omits runtime execution checks.

## What the results support

The paper reports zero policy violations in the tested decoder cells and high compliant-output coverage. These figures do not imply correct answers: weaker-model execution accuracy can decrease, and compliant alternatives on REFUSE-gold cases are not checked against intent-equivalent references.

## Limits and qualifications

Policy validity has only a 40-assignment author sanity check. Guarantees cover supported single-query column roles, excluding richer SQL, multi-query inference and broader privacy properties. Unsupported syntax or difficult planning can cause false refusal. Logits access is required, while token/call measurements omit wall-clock latency and masking overhead.

## Relevance to reliable Text-to-SQL

A concrete adjacent baseline for permission-dependent refusal and constrained answering. Its labels distinguish prohibited query uses from missing information, ambiguous intent or proof that no valid answer exists.
